citation: Schmidt, R. A., Pilchen, A. R., Laguarda, K., Wang, H., & Patel, D. (2020). Scaling up teacher induction: Implementation and impact on teachers and students (Evaluation of the New Teacher Center's i3 Scale-up Grant, Final Report). Menlo Park, CA: SRI International.
report_number: ERIC ED610347; SRI International final report for U.S. Dept. of Education Investing in Innovation (i3) scale-up grant to the New Teacher Center (#U411A150005-15A)
design: Cluster-randomized controlled trial; assignment level = School (schools randomized to treatment vs control within blocks defined by site/grades-served, 50% assignment probability, two random-assignment waves summer 2016 and 2017); 301 schools across 5 large urban districts (anonymized: Hayes Park, Fillmore County, Chesterton, Taftville, Garfield City) serving high proportions of students of color and low-income students; intervention = New Teacher Center (NTC) comprehensive teacher-induction model (intensive instructionally focused coaching for first/second-year teachers, mentor training, coaching tools, district capacity-building) vs business-as-usual district induction; outcomes = state standardized assessments in mathematics and ELA, grades 4-8 (grade 3 excluded for lack of prior-year score); impact analysis = 3-level HLM (students within teachers within schools) with site fixed effects and student/teacher/school covariates incl. prior-year test score.
problems:
GRADE-BAND DISCREPANCY: the registry codes this row as grade 3-6, but the report's confirmatory student-achievement analysis covers grades 4-8 (students were tested in grades 3-8; grade 3 was dropped because the model requires a prior-year score). The grade bands overlap (grades 4-6) but are not identical; no grade-3-6-only subgroup analysis is reported, so the extracted effect sizes are for the full grades-4-8 analysis sample.

NO STANDARD ERRORS REPORTED: Exhibit 22 (and Appendix D/G) report only the impact coefficient and a two-tailed p value, not the SE. I derived impact_se from the p value using the large-sample normal approximation SE = |impact| / qnorm(1 - p/2) (justified by ~7,000-8,000 students and 107-117 clusters): Math z(0.74)=0.332 -> SE=0.060; ELA z(0.50)=0.674 -> SE=0.044. These SEs (and the g_se/g_var derived from them) are reconstructions from p values, not directly reported numbers.

ELA EFFECT-SIZE INCONSISTENCY IN SOURCE: Exhibit 22 lists ELA impact=0.03, pooled SD=0.98, but reported 'Effect size'=0.05. 0.03/0.98=0.031, not 0.05, so the report's own ELA row is internally inconsistent (likely rounding of an underlying impact coefficient nearer 0.05, or a typo). I used the reported standardized impact coefficient (0.03) as the basis for g (g=0.031), and noted the published ES=0.05 in the per-effect notes. The math row is internally consistent (0.02/0.97=0.021, reported ES 0.02).

NO ICC REPORTED: the design-effect intraclass correlation is not stated anywhere in the report. Because the impacts come from a multilevel (3-level) model they already account for clustering (cluster_adjusted=true), so a central cluster correction is not required; icc is left null (not guessed).

NULL-RESULT STUDY: NTC's induction model was not implemented with adequate fidelity at any of the five sites and there were no statistically significant impacts on student achievement (math p=0.74, ELA p=0.50), teacher practice, or teacher retention. Both achievement coefficients are small and positive.

effect_sizes.arm_label: NTC comprehensive induction model (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual district induction
effect_sizes.test_name: State standardized mathematics assessment (varies by district; scores standardized to district mean/SD, or sample mean/SD for Garfield City)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (one-year impact, spring of teachers' 2nd induction year; Cohort 1 2017-18, Cohort 2 2018-19)
effect_sizes.g_method: d = reported standardized impact coefficient / pooled SD = 0.02 / 0.97 = 0.0206 (scores already standardized to district mean/SD, so impact is in SD units; this equals the report's reported effect size 0.02). Hedges' g = J*d with J=1-3/(4*df-1), df=n_t+n_c-2=7010, J=0.99989 -> g=0.0206. impact_se derived from p=0.74 via normal approx SE_impact=|0.02|/qnorm(1-0.74/2)=0.0603; g_se=J*SE_impact/pooled_SD=0.0621; g_var=g_se^2=0.00386.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. 35, Exhibit 22 (impact, p, pooled SD, ES, n); p. 32-33 Exhibit 20 (n schools/teachers/students by condition); Appendix G p. G-5 Exhibit G-6 (adjusted mean_t)
effect_sizes.notes: Confirmatory math achievement outcome. Reported impact 0.02 (p=0.74), reported effect size 0.02, pooled SD 0.97; not statistically significant. n_t/n_c = included students by condition from Exhibit 20 (treatment 3,801; control 3,211; total 7,012 matches Exhibit 22). n_clusters=107 included schools (math). Adjusted treatment mean -0.04 from Exhibit G-6 (adjusted control -0.06; both standardized, near 0). Sensitivity tests (Exhibit D-2) ranged -0.01 to 0.08, all non-significant.
